rationale: The same miracle told independently: five loaves and two fish, grass, about five thousand men, a blessing or thanksgiving, everyone satisfied, and twelve baskets of pieces left over (John 6:9-13, BSB). The Greek basket word, kophinos, is the same in John 6:13 as in Matthew 14:20, Mark 6:43 and Luke 9:17 (Bible Hub parallel texts; the Cambridge Bible notes the same). The differences are real: in John, Jesus raises the question of bread first, with Philip (6:5-7); Andrew points to "a boy with five barley loaves" (6:9); the Passover is near (6:4); Jesus "gave thanks" and distributes (6:11) rather than giving through the disciples; He orders the pieces gathered "so that nothing will be wasted" (6:12); and the crowd wants to "make Him king by force" (6:15). Graded parallel/strong, following conn-matt8-centurion-luke7, because the core event and its numbers match while the frames differ. Ellicott and the Cambridge Bible (via Bible Hub) call it the only miracle recorded by all four Evangelists; Wikipedia, a tertiary source, adds "aside from the resurrection."
